subject: Temporary SLO relief request for Inspector preview model
messages:
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@inspector.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary SLO relief request for Inspector preview model

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Inspector's team is excited about the latency characteristics of Redwood's serving runtime. We have a short-lived pilot planned next week to validate the new 'inspector-lite-v0' model as part of an in-product safety checker. The model is still experimental; early runs show higher p95 variability under realistic prompts.

We'd like to request a temporary SLO carveout for this preview launch (2 weeks) so our customer-facing service can ramp without triggering automated incident escalation. High-level ask: relax the latency SLO from p95 < 250ms to p95 < 600ms and allow a reduced uptime commitment (provisional availability target 98.0%) for the duration of the pilot. We'll limit traffic to a canary cohort (~2% of users) and will provide daily perf dumps so your team can monitor.

Attached: inspector_preview_perf_report.csv and the security questionnaire (partially complete). Procurement is copied for contracting cadence. Can you confirm whether Redwood can approve a provisional SLO variance, and if there are any requirements on capacity reservation or additional fees?

Cheers,
Sam Lee
Head of Integrations
Inspector.ai

Attachments: inspector_preview_perf_report.csv (csv), inspector_security_qs.pdf (pdf)
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@inspector.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary SLO relief request for Inspector preview model

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the perf CSV. High level: I'm supportive of enabling a short, controlled SLO variance for preview beta work, but we'll need to formalize a few items before sign-off. Quick questions/notes: 

- Can you confirm the expected qps and average payload size during the canary? (we need this for capacity reservations)
- We'll want daily P95/P99 exports in a standard JSON lines format; our Ops team will ingest those into the incident dashboard.
- SLO carveouts typically require: (1) a signed mutual action plan (MAP) describing traffic thresholds and rollback criteria, (2) an agreed end date (we can do rolling 7-day renewals), and (3) optional reserved capacity if you expect sustained spike.

Marissa — looping you in for deal and procurement coordination. Markus — FYI on the ingestion/monitoring requirements and whether we should suggest a dedicated slot on a d-pool for the canary.

I can draft a short MAP today and propose a conservative window (2 weeks, with option to extend once we see stability). If procurement is willing to accept a provisional addendum, we can move quickly.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Signed MAP (I attached a draft — inspector_map_draft.docx) with traffic caps, rollback triggers, and data retention limits.
- Confirmation whether Inspector wants Redwood to reserve dedicated capacity for the pilot (this will affect pricing).

If Procurement is comfortable, we can attach the MAP to a limited addendum (1-2 pages) and target execution by EOD tomorrow. Logan — can your draft include the monitoring schema and the export schedule? Markus — please advise whether we should require a hot standby pool for the first 48 hours.
